candidate.answerReason: The hexagon has area \(54\sqrt{3}\), and the six nonoverlapping corner sectors have total area \(18\pi\). Their difference matches choice C.

methods.label: Subtract the six corner sectors
methods.explanation:
The shaded region is what remains after removing the six corner sectors from the hexagon. Joining the hexagon's center to its vertices splits it into six congruent triangles. Their central angles are \(360^\circ/6=60^\circ\), and their two radial sides are equal, so the triangles are equilateral with side length \(6\).

An altitude of one triangle divides its base into two segments of length \(3\). By the Pythagorean theorem, its height is
\[
h=\sqrt{6^2-3^2}=3\sqrt{3}.
\]
Thus the hexagon's area is
\[
6\left(\frac12\cdot6\cdot3\sqrt{3}\right)=54\sqrt{3}.
\]
Two \(60^\circ\) triangle angles meet at each hexagon vertex, so each corner sector has angle \(120^\circ\). Its radius is \(3\), giving area
\[
\frac{120}{360}\pi\cdot3^2=3\pi.
\]
Adjacent sector centers are \(6=3+3\) units apart, so those sectors only touch. Nonadjacent vertices are \(6\sqrt{3}\) or \(12\) units apart, so their sectors cannot overlap. We may therefore subtract all six sector areas once:
\[
54\sqrt{3}-6(3\pi)=\boxed{54\sqrt{3}-18\pi}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
